claims.text: An actively learned and cross-validated machine-learning interatomic potential can accurately reproduce ab initio free-energy surfaces for both solid and liquid phases near melting.
Transfer learning can refine an ML potential so that it captures electron–vibration coupling.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by at least an order of magnitude relative to explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD workflows.
Elemental aluminum is a well-characterized benchmark with known free-energy surfaces.
ML interatomic potentials can approximate the underlying DFT energy landscape with near-DFT energy and force accuracy.
Active learning can tailor an MLIP training set to a target system and property while reducing the amount of required DFT data.
Sparse representative AIMD training data collected from 0.9Tm to 1.1Tm are sufficient to cover solid and liquid configurations accurately.
Atomic-displacement correlations carry information needed for accurate vibrational-entropy estimates.
The proposed ML potential will retain the atomic-displacement correlations needed for free-energy calculations.
The proposed ML potential will retain local electronic effects, including electron–vibration coupling.
Active learning can preferentially identify the regions of phase space most important to entropy contributions.
The trained potential will capture anharmonic effects, vibrational entropy, and electron–vibration coupling in both phases.
Cross-validation against AIMD and transfer-learning corrections will ensure reliability across both solid and liquid states.
Enhanced-sampling thermodynamic integration with the ML potential will efficiently compute solid and liquid free energies.
The method will predict phase free energies and latent heat with fidelity approximating explicit AIMD.
Multicomponent high-entropy alloys will particularly benefit from the proposed cost reduction.
Explicit AIMD free-energy evaluations and TOR-TILD are computationally intensive, especially for multicomponent alloys.
The approach is applicable to elemental, binary, and multicomponent high-entropy systems over approximately 0.9Tm to 1.1Tm.
